correctness.rationale: Baadi's real-coefficient Theorem 1.2 states for every \(q\in(1,2]\) that \(p_-(\mathcal H)<q\) iff \(\omega\in RH_{q'/2}\), and the same introduction explicitly lists the power-weight condition \(-2n/q'<\beta<n\). For \(\beta<0\), solving that inequality gives \(q>2n/(2n+\beta)\); the infimum in the source definition is therefore exactly that value. The local-finiteness clause gives the identical boundary because \(|x|^{\beta p'/2}\) is locally integrable iff \(\beta p'/2>-n\). For \(\beta\ge0\), the source explicitly places the power weight in \(RH_\infty\), and its real-coefficient theorem gives \(p_-=1\). Substitution into the source Riesz and duality ranges is algebraically correct. At \(\beta=-n^2/(n+2)\), direct algebra gives \(p_-=2_*\) while the endpoint power \(|x|^{-n}\) in the reverse-Hölder test is not locally integrable. The packaged symbolic checker correctly replays these identities.
